Nina: Quick - discovered an automation gap. Pricing experiment credits applied as one-line invoice discounts in Nov but audit wants them tracked as deferred marketing credits impacting revrec. What's the guidance?
Omar: Are these customer-specific promotional credits or platform-wide grants?
Nina: Customer-specific: three pilot customers, total invoice discount $9,600, tied to a Q4 pricing test. Service ran Nov-Jan. Booked as invoice discounts at billing time (reduced revenue in Oct invoice).
Eileen: For audit, if the credit is considered a marketing incentive that amortizes as the service is delivered, it should be presented as contra-revenue on the amortization schedule. So record deferral gross then recognize net of credit.
Sam: Does that require opening an adjusting journal to move the reduction from invoice line to a deferred contra-revenue account?
Nina: Proposed: reverse the invoice discount impact and record deferred promo liability:
Dr 4001-Revenue reduction reversal 9,600
Cr 3100-DeferredPromoCredit 9,600
Then amortize contra-revenue 3,200/mo alongside service revenue.
FinanceBot: Draft JE FIN-5012 created by Nina (status: pending).
Omar: Make sure the memo links pricing experiment ID and A/B cohort tags. Auditors will ask for segmentation.
Nina: Will attach experiment notes and cohort lists to FIN-5012.
